purpose: Read-only peer-review recommendations for the six new PHEVs. This file is an audit record, not an automatically applied rating override.
target: One rear-facing child restraint plus two forward-facing restraints or boosters. The family's Maxi-Cosi model is unknown; no published test confirms their personal fit.
method: Primary article text and the actual linked photographs were inspected. A three-forward-facing picture plus a separate rear-facing legroom claim is not proof of the simultaneous target arrangement. ANCAP individual installation checks do not prove three-across fit or daily booster buckle access.

observations.visualFinding: The inspected three-across photographs show two rear-facing convertibles plus one forward-facing booster.
observations.textFinding: The review names an Infasecure Optima, Serene and Versatile Folding Booster and says the convertibles fitted in either direction. A 180 cm driver or 184 cm passenger fitted ahead of a rear-facing restraint. Loading from inside and outside was described as easy.
observations.reason: Useful mixed-direction and alternate-direction evidence, but the exact one-rear-facing/two-other layout is not documented simultaneously. Do not treat the two-rear-facing picture as proof of the requested layout while excluding equivalent evidence for existing cars.

observations.visualFinding: Photos 40 and 42 show three forward-facing harnessed seats. The side-on rear-facing photo 36 shows both outer seats rear-facing; it does not document the requested one-rear-facing mix.
observations.textFinding: The review names two Infasecure Achieve More and one Attain More and says they fitted forward or rear-facing. A 184 cm driver fitted ahead of rear-facing; door openings and inside loading were described favourably.
observations.reason: The prose supports direction flexibility, but no inspected picture or explicit statement records one rear-facing plus two other seats simultaneously. The tested Exceed is related to the listed Aspire.

observations.testedVehicle: H6 PHEV in June 2026 roundup; grade not named
observations.visualFinding: The inspected H6 roundup image shows the boot and pram, not an installed child-seat arrangement.
observations.textFinding: The first-person roundup separately reports three-across fit and room for a 182 cm driver ahead of a rear-facing restraint; restraint models and simultaneous direction mix are not specified.

additionalRelatedTest.finding: Both H6GT PHEV photos clearly show one rear-facing infant capsule plus two forward-facing harnessed seats. This is a different coupe body and AWD configuration, not direct proof for the listed regular-body H6 Lux FWD. Keep the distinction visible if used as related context.

observations.reason: Manufacturer anchor locations or a five-seat body do not measure child-loading access. The H6GT evidence cannot silently become an exact regular-H6 fit claim.

observations.testedVehicle: 2026 Geely Starray EM-i Inspire, tested December 2025
observations.visualFinding: The actual photograph clearly shows one rear-facing convertible plus two forward-facing harnessed seats. The article also explicitly states this combination was tried.
observations.textFinding: Three-across shoulder space was tight; the driver ahead of rear-facing could be 186 cm. A flat rear floor helped movement around the child seats.
observations.reason: Related Inspire evidence supports the requested direction mix, with a width limitation. One ANCAP centre-booster installation failure is a useful compatibility warning, not evidence of poor daily buckle access. Retain the warning separately.

observations.testedVehicle: Chery Tiggo 7 PHEV in June 2026 roundup; grade not named
observations.visualFinding: The actual three-across photograph shows three forward-facing restraints, not one rear-facing plus two others.
observations.textFinding: The roundup separately reports room for a 180 cm driver ahead of a rear-facing restraint. It does not name a simultaneous mixed-direction arrangement or the tested grade.
observations.reason: Keep the genuine three-forward-facing and rear-facing clearance findings visible. Manufacturer anchor hardware and a normal two-row layout do not establish child-loading access.

observations.visualFinding: Both inspected child-seat/legroom photographs show three forward-facing restraints.
observations.textFinding: Three-across fit was tight. The separate rear-facing legroom test limited driver height to about 162 cm. Reaching row three required removing one second-row restraint; row three has no ISOFIX or top tethers.
observations.reason: The article discusses seats in either direction, but the inspected evidence does not document one rear-facing plus two others simultaneously. Keep the strong, relevant legroom and third-row-access drawbacks without turning an unverified target arrangement into a numerical score.
